# n2 - The graph tree renderer (melds 327a)

`GraphTree.render(edges:, labels:, marks:, width:)` draws any edge map as an indented tree with
box-drawing branches: a node may have any number of children, and a node several branches need is
drawn once at the point where those branches join. It marks the critical path and the ready set.
Pure, plain text, no roadmap knowledge, so the same renderer serves the roadmap file, the roadmap
screens, and later the node scope.

## n2 failure-mode matrix
| Row | Operation | Failure mode | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2.1 | Draw a linear chain with each need above its dependent | Melded at review (A12): a dependent drawn above the thing it needs makes the reader start at the leaf and plan the work backwards | `graph_tree_test#test_chain_renders_each_need_above_its_dependent` |
| 2.2 | Draw a shared dependency once, where the branches join | A node two branches need is drawn under each branch, so a reader counts the same work twice and plans two deliveries of one intent | `graph_tree_test#test_shared_dependency_is_drawn_once_at_the_join` |
| 2.3 | Draw fan-in from three or more roots | Only the first root is joined and the other two are dropped from the drawing, so the tree understates what blocks the head | `graph_tree_test#test_three_roots_all_join_into_their_common_head` |
| 2.4 | Order children deterministically, by batch then id | Two renders of the same input differ, so every render dirties the roadmap file and the diff is noise forever | `graph_tree_test#test_same_input_renders_byte_identical_twice` |
| 2.5 | Mark the critical path | The long pole is unmarked or marked on a shorter chain, and the one fact the drawing exists to answer is wrong | `graph_tree_test#test_critical_path_is_marked_on_the_longest_chain_only` |
| 2.6 | Mark the ready set | Entries that can start now are unmarked, so the reader still has to compute readiness by hand and the tree buys nothing | `graph_tree_test#test_ready_entries_are_marked_and_blocked_ones_are_not` |
| 2.7 | Emit no escape byte | An ANSI sequence is written into a roadmap file on disk, where it corrupts the markdown and every non-terminal reader | `graph_tree_test#test_output_contains_no_escape_byte` |
| 2.8 | Fit a long label to the given width | A long intent title runs past the width and the box-drawing columns break, so the tree stops being readable exactly when it is largest | `graph_tree_test#test_long_label_is_truncated_to_the_width_and_columns_stay_aligned` |
| 2.9 | Render an empty edge map | The renderer raises or emits a stray glyph on a roadmap that has a graph section with no edges | `graph_tree_test#test_empty_graph_renders_a_named_empty_line` |
| 2.10 | Refuse a cyclic edge map | The walk recurses forever and the render hangs the screen, the writer, and the doctor run that called it | `graph_tree_test#test_cyclic_edges_are_refused_with_the_path_and_do_not_hang` |
| 2.11 | Fall back to the id when a node has no label | The row renders blank, so a node the graph names has no visible identity in the drawing | `graph_tree_test#test_node_without_a_label_renders_its_id` |
| 2.12 | Render a node that is both a root and a leaf | An isolated entry is dropped from the tree entirely, so work with no edges vanishes from the drawing | `graph_tree_test#test_isolated_node_still_appears` |
| 2.13 | Keep the renderer free of a clock and an environment seam | The renderer reads `Time.now` or an env var and becomes unreproducible. Melded at review (A11): stated as a hermeticity guard, not a determinism proof, which row 2.4 owns | `graph_tree_test#test_library_source_reads_no_clock_or_environment` |
| 2.14 | Place a shared node by a stated rule | Melded at review (B8): with the placement rule undefined for `n3 needs n1 n2`, the executor invents one and pins it in a test. The rule: a node is drawn under its highest-batch need, ties broken by smallest id, with its other needs shown as converging references at the join | `graph_tree_test#test_shared_node_hangs_under_its_highest_batch_need_ties_by_smallest_id` |
